'''R4-D6''' was a dark [[Color|blue]] [[R4 astromech droid|R4 astromech]] [[droid]]<ref name="Disney Infinity">''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''</ref> that served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. During the [[Battle of Yavin]] it was present in the hangar bay of the [[Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4]], a structure being used as the headquarters of the Alliance. It rolled beneath the snout of an [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]] being prepared to attack the Imperial [[Death Star]] [[superweapon]] as the [[Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker]] and the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] argued about whether Solo was staying to aid the Alliance in the coming battle.<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
R4-D6 first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="ANH" /> The droid was then first identified in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', which was released in [[2008]].<ref name="Complete Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The name was then first used in [[canon]] by the video game ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'' when it was released on [[August 30]], [[2015]].<ref name="Disney Infinity" /> Despite the game's non-canon status, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] confirmed on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] that the names it uses for film characters are considered canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/749616406245699584|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2016-07-03|quote=@LelalMekha Yeah, same with Infinity.|archivefile=File:PabloHidalgo-LegoName-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "@pablohidalgo <nowiki>youtube.com/watch?v=JwxAeHPLpPg</nowiki> The Lego game identifies a few BG characters from TFA, but are those names canonical?"}}</ref>
